issues.title: Inverted conditional logic in setUserFeatureState causes wrong branch execution
issues.description: The conditional check for handling the 'inherit' state has been inverted from `if (state === 'inherit')` to `if (state !== 'inherit')`. This causes the method to incorrectly pass the state without assignedBy when state is 'enabled' or 'disabled', and incorrectly attempts to access assignedBy property (which doesn't exist in the union type) when state is 'inherit', leading to runtime TypeScript errors and incorrect database operations. When users try to enable/disable a feature, the assignedBy tracking will be lost, and when they set it to inherit, the code will crash trying to access a non-existent property.

issues.title: Missing await in setUserState mutation causes race condition
issues.description: The await keyword was removed from the featureOptInService.setUserFeatureState call in the tRPC mutation handler. This causes the mutation to return success immediately without waiting for the database operation to complete, creating a race condition where the response is sent before the state is actually persisted. Users will receive success responses even if the underlying operation fails, and subsequent reads might not reflect the changes they just made, leading to inconsistent UI state and data integrity issues.

issues.title: Inverted filter logic in listFeaturesForUser returns disabled features instead of enabled
issues.description: The filter condition in listFeaturesForUser was changed from `filter((state) => state.globalEnabled)` to `filter((state) => !state.globalEnabled)`, inverting the logic. This causes the method to return only globally disabled features instead of enabled ones. Users will see an empty or incorrect list of available features in their settings UI, as only features that are globally disabled (which should be hidden) will be shown, while actually available features will be filtered out. This breaks the entire feature opt-in UI for users.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26801 - feat: add scope configuration for feature opt-in

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an optional `scope` field (`org` / `team` / `user`) to opt-in feature configs. It adds helpers to filter features by scope and to check scope access, filters the list endpoints by scope, rejects mutations outside a feature's scope with `ErrorWithCode(BadRequest)`, and uses a separate visibility constant for each scope in the settings sidebar. The overall design is sound and backward-compatible: a feature with no `scope` shows up everywhere.

Along the way, though, the diff introduces several regressions that break core behavior. `listFeaturesForUser` now returns only features that are globally *disabled*. `setUserFeatureState` has its branches swapped, so enable/disable writes go out without `assignedBy`, and Prisma rejects them because the column is required. The `setUserState` tRPC mutation also lost its `await`, so those failures turn into unhandled rejections while the client is told `{ success: true }`. The new unit tests mock both scope helpers, so they never check the real scope logic. There's also a leftover unused constant in `config.ts`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Three correctness regressions break user-level opt-in: the inverted globalEnabled filter, the swapped inherit branches, and the missing await. Together they mean users see the wrong features and can't save opt-in changes, and the UI still reports success.

architecture.overview:
Opt-in features are declared statically in `feature-opt-in/config.ts` (`OPT_IN_FEATURES`). The tRPC `featureOptInRouter` exposes list and set endpoints for the user, team and organization levels. These go through `FeatureOptInService`, which calls `FeaturesRepository` to work with the `UserFeatures` / `TeamFeatures` tables. Orgs are stored as teams, so org endpoints reuse the team methods.

This PR adds an `OptInFeatureScope` type and an optional `scope` array on each config entry, plus two helpers: `getOptInFeaturesForScope` and `isFeatureAllowedForScope`. The service filters list results by scope, and the router passes `scope: "team"` or `"org"` explicitly. The set methods now check scope before writing and throw `ErrorWithCode(BadRequest)` when a feature isn't allowed. The settings sidebar replaces the single `HAS_OPT_IN_FEATURES` flag with one flag per scope, so the Features tab appears only where at least one feature applies.
steps: Start in `packages/features/feature-opt-in/types.ts` and `config.ts`: the new `OptInFeatureScope` type, the `scope?` field, the `HAS_*_OPT_IN_FEATURES` flags and the two scope helpers.
Read `SettingsLayoutAppDirClient.tsx`: each settings section (my-account, organization, team list) now checks its own scope flag before showing the Features tab.
Follow `featureOptInRouter` (`_router.ts`): the list endpoints pass `scope: "team"` / `"org"`, and `setTeamState` / `setOrganizationState` pass the scope to the service.

In `FeatureOptInService.ts`, `listFeaturesForUser` / `listFeaturesForTeam` now iterate only over scoped features, and both set methods call `isFeatureAllowedForScope` before delegating to `FeaturesRepository`.
Finish with the tests: the unit tests mock the config helpers, and the integration test forces `isFeatureAllowedForScope` to return true.

findings.title: listFeaturesForUser now returns only globally disabled features
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.ts` line 207, `listFeaturesForUser` filters with `!state.globalEnabled`, so it returns only globally disabled features. Change the predicate to `state.globalEnabled` to match the doc comment and `listFeaturesForTeam`. Then add a unit test in `FeatureOptInService.test.ts` for `listFeaturesForUser`, mocking `getAllFeatures` with one enabled and one disabled feature, and assert that only the enabled one is returned.

findings.title: setUserFeatureState branches are swapped, so enable/disable writes lose assignedBy
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.ts` around line 264, `setUserFeatureState` checks `state !== "inherit"`, which swaps the branches. Enable/disable calls go out without `assignedBy`, and Prisma rejects them because `UserFeatures.assignedBy` is required. Restore `if (state === "inherit")` so the inherit branch omits `assignedBy` and the else branch passes `assignedBy: `user-${assignedBy}``, matching `setTeamFeatureState`. Run `FeatureOptInService.test.ts` to confirm the setUserFeatureState tests pass.

findings.title: Missing await on setUserFeatureState in setUserState mutation
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/featureOptIn/_router.ts` line 103, the `setUserState` mutation calls `featureOptInService.setUserFeatureState(...)` without `await`. It returns success before the write completes, and errors, including the new scope-validation BadRequest, become unhandled rejections. Add `await`, matching `setTeamState` and `setOrganizationState` in the same file.

findings.title: Unit tests mock away the scope logic they claim to cover
findings.body:
The config mock replaces both new helpers:

::code{file="packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.test.ts" lines="12-27"}

- `getOptInFeaturesForScope` always returns all five features, whatever scope it's given. The listFeaturesForTeam tests then assert that `org-only-feature`, `user-only-feature` and the rest are all queried for a team. That locks in the opposite of the intended filtering.
- `isFeatureAllowedForScope` is a `vi.fn()` whose return value each test sets directly. The "not allowed at X scope" tests only check that the service throws when the mock says false. Pass `"user-only-feature"` with `scope: "user"` and they'd still throw.

The real `scope.includes(...)` and default-to-all-scopes logic in `config.ts` has no tests at all.

::callout{type="warning"}
The mock fixtures also lack `policy`, so they don't match `OptInFeatureConfig`.

Two better options: make the mock's helpers apply the real filtering over `mockFeatures`, or test `getOptInFeaturesForScope` / `isFeatureAllowedForScope` directly in a `config.test.ts` and drop the mock for those functions.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/services/FeatureOptInService.test.ts` (lines 12-27), `getOptInFeaturesForScope` is mocked to return every feature and `isFeatureAllowedForScope` is a bare `vi.fn`, so no test checks the real scope filtering. Make the mock implement the real logic over `mockFeatures`, i.e. `(scope) => mockFeatures.filter(f => !f.scope || f.scope.includes(scope))`, and similarly for `isFeatureAllowedForScope`. Update the listFeaturesForTeam expectations so team scope excludes org-only and user-only features. Add a `listForTeam` test with `scope: "org"`. Also add `packages/features/feature-opt-in/config.test.ts` to test the helpers directly, covering features with no scope, a single scope, and unknown slugs.

findings.title: Leftover unused constant in config.ts
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/feature-opt-in/config.ts` lines 4-5, delete the `UNUSED_CONSTANT` declaration and its comment. Optionally, define `HAS_USER/TEAM/ORG_OPT_IN_FEATURES` as `getOptInFeaturesForScope(scope).length > 0` so the scope predicate isn't duplicated, and either use `ALL_SCOPES` or remove it.

findings.title: Backward-compatible scope design with server-side enforcement
findings.body: Making `scope` optional and treating a missing value as all scopes keeps existing configs working. Enforcing scope in the service, not just hiding UI tabs, is the right boundary. `isFeatureAllowedForScope` also rejects unknown slugs, which is a safe default. Having one sidebar flag per scope means the Features tab won't show up on pages where nothing can be configured.
